teaching.hint: How does a repeated neighboring color affect all groups ending at that position?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: A window alternates exactly when the alternating suffix ending there has length at least k; circular starts correspond to a precise finite range of unrolled endpoints.
solution_outline.approach: Read positions 0 through n+k-2 using circular indices. Track the current alternating run length, resetting to one at equal neighbors. Count endpoints k-1 through n+k-2 whose run reaches k.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The run length is the longest alternating suffix in the unrolled prefix. Each counted endpoint corresponds to one starting position in 0..n-1.
solution_outline.correctness: A length-k group is alternating exactly when all its k-1 internal edges change color, equivalent to a suffix run of at least k. Start s maps uniquely to endpoint s+k-1. The endpoint range covers precisely all n starts, so the scan includes wrapped groups once each and imposes no additional closing-edge condition.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n+k)=O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
solution_outline.pitfall: Unrolling a full second copy and counting every qualifying endpoint can count some starts twice; use the exact endpoint range.

common_wrong_turns: Unrolling a full second copy and counting every qualifying endpoint can count some starts twice; use the exact endpoint range.
source_fidelity_notes: Replaced diagrams with explicit internal adjacency, full-length group semantics, and occurrence counting by circular start.
